front.title: Signed Policy Conferral and Population Distribution with an Exclusion Proof

abstract.t: This memo specifies signed policy conferral, a way to distribute an enforceable defensive policy to a population of recipients. A conferral envelope carries a policy artefact that a recipient applies, a signature block that needs a quorum of independent signers, an exclusion proof that the policy does not carry the sensitive method or data it was derived from, and a staged-rollout directive that confines the first distribution to a bounded cohort. The envelope travels as the payload of a conferral frame kind that this memo defines for the identity-keyed fan-out frame of the agent- channel fan-out memo, and its signers sign with COSE or JOSE. It introduces no new transport and no new signature format. The memo covers the many-recipient case that the briefing-and-binding envelope memo excludes from its scope. It differs from the Common Security Advisory Framework, which standardises advisory documents for a recipient to read, by distributing a signed policy for a recipient to apply.
